title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed (mimeographed) sheet from a Bourbaki draft, 'n° 392', page '6 - 24'. It sits in cote 60 between handwritten pages on traces of inertia invariants and L-series. Most likely it is recycled paper: Grothendieck's notes would be on the verso, or the sheet was simply filed there. The content is a set of exercises on Krull and factorial rings, matching the exercises of Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative, Ch. VII (Diviseurs), §3.

(4a) A = Q[X,Y]/(X^2+Y^2-1) is a Krull domain, being a normal noetherian domain. It is not factorial. The image of X is irreducible ('extrémal'), but A/XA ≅ Q[Y]/(Y^2-1) ≅ Q×Q is not a domain, so XA is not prime.

(4b) After extending scalars to Q(i), set U = X+iY and V = X-iY. This gives A⊗Q(i) ≅ Q(i)[U,V]/(UV-1) ≅ Q(i)[U,U^{-1}], a Laurent polynomial ring, hence factorial. This shows factoriality does not descend from Q(i) to Q.

(5a) Let g = X1X2 - Σ g_i(X3..Xn) X1^i with g0 prime. Then B/gB is factorial. Proof idea: invert X1. Then S^{-1}A ≅ k[X1, X1^{-1}, X3, ..., Xn] is factorial. Apply Nagata's criterion (the 'prop. 3 du n° 4'), using that X1 is prime in A because A/X1A ≅ k[X2..Xn]/(g0).

(5b) A nondegenerate quadratic form F in n ≥ 5 variables over a field of characteristic ≠ 2 gives a factorial ring k[X]/(F) (the Klein–Nagata theorem). Over an algebraically closed field, change variables to F = X1X2 - G(X3..Xn). Here G is a nondegenerate form in n-2 ≥ 3 variables, hence irreducible. Then apply (5a) and descend via Exercise 3b.

(5c) For X1X2 - X3X4, the four X_i are pairwise non-associate irreducibles with X1X2 = X3X4, so the ring is not factorial.

(6a, 6b) Over an ordered field with a, b, c > 0, the ring k[X,Y,Z]/(aX^2+bY^2+cZ^2) is factorial. The method: reduce to a real closed field, then show every graded height-one prime is principal. Over the algebraic closure, graded height-one primes correspond to points of the conic; conjugate pairs give principal ideals generated by linear forms. Then use the graded criterion (Ex. 3a). This is Samuel's example, x^2+y^2+z^2 over R being factorial.

None of this connects to the surrounding material on L-functions or inertia invariants.
errors: In 4a the hint says 'AX n'est pas un idéal maximal'. What is needed, and true, is that AX is not a prime ideal: A/AX ≅ Q×Q. This is probably a typo or draft slip for 'premier'. It is not maximal either, but 'not maximal' alone would not prove non-factoriality.
In 5c one must also check that the X_i are pairwise non-associate. This is implicit and easy.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed Bourbaki draft sheet (n° 392) of standard exercises on factorial rings, all published in Bourbaki AC VII. It is unrelated to the L-function notes around it and contains nothing by Grothendieck that is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: 'Q' denotes the rational field ℚ, and Q(i) denotes ℚ(i).
'6 - 24 -' is a draft page number, and 'n° 392' is the Bourbaki redaction number. The handwritten '43' is the archive folio number.
